newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo residents hide Hutu refugees from Alliance.
newsitem.headline: Congo residents hide Hutu refugees from Alliance.

text.p: A civil servant in the new Democratic Republic of Congo sidled up to a U.N. aid worker and whispered: "If somebody was hiding refugees, could they bring them to you without being caught?"
Residents of the western town of Mbandaka on the Congo River are playing a deadly game of hide and seek with troops from the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL).
They are hiding refugees from AFDL soldiers and say they fear that they and the refugees could be killed if caught.

Witnesses say more than 200 unarmed Rwandan Hutu refugees were massacred by AFDL fighters on the quayside when the Alliance entered the town on May 13 and about 140 were killed by other AFDL troops at nearby Wendji village the same day.

Witnesses including priests, port officials and teachers told Reuters they saw the killings at the quay and Red Cross workers at Wendji said they had buried the 140 at the local cemetery and showed mass graves.
The civil servant, who declined to be named, finally admitted Friday his own family were hiding refugees near his home and asked the U.N. refugee agency to take them to safety.
Refugee Godeberthe Mujawamaria, a former secretary from the Rwandan capital Kigali, sat on a stool with three girls and a baby in the yard at the back of the house.
She said she fled into the bush when shooting began on May 13 and remained in hiding during the day fed by local people.
"The people told me that they (Alliance troops) would kill Rwandan refugees if they found them so that is why I am hiding," Mujawamaria said.
The civil servant's mother said she discovered the Hutu family only when the children started to cry.

"When the children started to cry, their mother came out and asked me for something to eat. I was afraid because I heard the soldiers were killing those who hid Rwandans," the civil servant's mother said.
"I was afraid to help but there was a force inside me that made me help them...Whenever I made something to eat I would prepare a little extra for them, cassava, maize or water," she said.

The AFDL has denied exterminating Rwandan Hutu refugees in Mbandaka or during its seven-month thrust across Zaire, renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo when the Alliance's leader Laurent Kabila proclaimed himself president on May 17.
"Everybody is doing all they can to help these people (refugees) and I want to thank UNHCR for bringing in a plane to repatriate them," said the newly elected Mbandaka governor, Gabriel Mula Mutya.

The Hutu refugees, who trekked some 1,200 km (750 miles) across the former Zaire in six months, fled Rwanda in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The U.N. refugee agency started an operation in Mbandaka last week to find and fly home what local authorities say could as many as 20,000 Rwandan refugees who fled into the bush.
Mujawamaria and the children were loaded into a van and driven to a U.N. collection centre to await repatriation.
"This woman has done something very good. If you find refugees you must bring them to us," UNHCR spokesman Peter Kessler told a crowd of onlookers.
"What happened to the refugees (the killings) has never happened in Mbandaka before. It has traumatised the entire population," the civil servant said.
Others said life was better since the Alliance takeover.

"The FAZ (Zairean government army) mistreated us and when the Alliance came, it was a liberation and frankly it is better, but the thing that has shocked everyone is the way they have treated our brothers the refugees," said a local priest.
